citations.note: Zhu, Paths maximize the expected range of graph-indexed random walks; includes K_{2,3} example but no general K_{a,b} formula found in inspected text.

evidence: The enumerations are correct. With a root in the A-part, standard height functions have B-values in {±1}; if both signs appear then A is forced to zero, while a constant B sign gives two choices on each non-root A vertex. This yields N_H=2^a+2^b-2 and exactly two range-one functions. For the lazy model, partitioning by the exact subset of {-1,0,1} used on B gives N_L=3^a+3^b+2^(a+b)-2^(a+1)-2^(b+1)+1. Diameter two bounds the range; inclusion-exclusion for images contained in {0,1} or {-1,0} gives 2^(a+b)-2 range-one functions. The expectation formulas follow. The fixed-order extrema follow from strict discrete convexity of 2^k and F(k)=3^k-2^(k+1). Independent brute-force enumeration on small (a,b), including K_{2,3}, reproduced every range coefficient.

independent_checks: Re-derived the standard and lazy counts by conditioning on the exact set of B-part heights.
Verified the range-one inclusion-exclusion count and resulting expectations.
Checked strict discrete convexity and both star/balanced asymptotics.
Independently enumerated several small complete bipartite graphs and matched all coefficients.
limitations: The theorem is specific to complete bipartite graphs and the two uniform rooted height-function models.
The full older 2000 and 2003 articles were not both inspected line-by-line, leaving residual risk of an unindexed elementary special-case enumeration.
Finite enumeration supports but does not replace the general proof.

evidence: Zhu's 2026 paper studies the global path-extremality problem and uses K_{2,3} as an example, but the inspected open full text did not state a general K_{a,b} range enumerator. Earlier Benjamini--Häggström--Mossel and Loebl--Nešetřil--Reed establish the standard/lazy models and general theory. Targeted searches for the exact complete-bipartite formulas and repository history did not locate an earlier equivalent result. The novelty claim is therefore limited to the closed K_{a,b} range laws and their fixed-order extremal consequences, not the models or path bounds.

The result gives a complete solvable family that sharply contrasts balanced bicliques and stars in the lazy model, including different asymptotic expected ranges. It also supplies an exact benchmark for the recent extremal theory, so the scientific value is more than a one-off count.
